criteria_quotes:
Total shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary for joint disease when ALL of the following criteria are met:
• There is a documented diagnosis of one of the following:
  o Degenerative joint disease (DJD)
  o Osteoarthritis (OA)
  o Rheumatoid arthritis (RA)
  o Traumatic arthritis
  o Avascular necrosis
AND
• Treatment is needed because of one or more of the following:
  o Disabling pain for at least 3 months duration
  o Functional disability which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living for at least 3 months duration
AND
• Radiographic or imaging evidence (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI) of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by ONE or more of the following:
  o Irregular joint surfaces
  o Glenoid sclerosis
  o Glenoid osteophyte changes
  o Flattened glenoid
  o Cystic changes in the humeral head
  o Joint space narrowing
AND
• Documentation of three months of failed non-operative conservative management as demonstrated by a trial of one or more of the following:
  o Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics
  o Intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate
AND
• A 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional:
  o Physical therapy
  o Activity modification
  o Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises

Total shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions:
• Proximal humerus fracture malunion or non-union
• Reconstruction after tumor resection of the glenohumeral joint or surrounding tissue
• Failed hemi-arthroplasty
• Post-traumatic injury (e.g., fracture, infection) causing shoulder joint destruction
answer.submission_route:
Submit a completed Member Appeal Form (or written statement) and supporting clinical documentation via one of the following channels:
- Mail: Premera Blue Cross, Member Appeals, PO Box 91102, Seattle, WA 98111-9202
- Fax: 425-918-5592
- Online: Sign in to your account at premera.com and select 'Secure Inbox' to send a secure message.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The clinical criteria are publicly available online at https://www.premera.com/medicalpolicies-individual/7.01.590.pdf. If needed, the patient can request a printed copy of the clinical criteria applied to their case by calling Premera Blue Cross Customer Service at the number listed on the back of their member ID card.
answer.notes: The denial specifically noted that 'the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity'. To successfully appeal, the provider must submit imaging reports (such as X-rays, CTs, or MRIs) taken within 12 months prior to the proposed surgery date that demonstrate at least one of the specific degenerative features required by the policy (irregular joint surfaces, glenoid sclerosis, glenoid osteophyte changes, flattened glenoid, cystic changes in the humeral head, or joint space narrowing).

Introduction Shoulder arthroplasty is when surgery is performed to replace the shoulder joint. The damaged part of the shoulder joint is removed, and metal and plastic parts are put in its place. A common reason for people to need this surgery is very bad pain from overuse, and not being able to do normal daily activities. Some people may need only a part of their shoulder replaced, which is when the shoulder head or ball is replaced with metal or plastic parts, but the socket is left as is. Sometimes the implanted parts need to be reversed. This is called reverse shoulder arthroplasty. This policy outlines when shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary. Note: The Introduction section is for your general knowledge and is not to be taken as policy coverage criteria. The rest of the policy uses specific words and concepts familiar to medical professionals. It is intended for providers. A provider can be a person, such as a doctor, nurse, psychologist, or dentist. A provider also can be a place where medical care is given, like a hospital, clinic, or lab. This policy informs them about when a service may be covered.
